title: Electrical Design Engineer
description:
Electrical Design Engineer

The Impact You’ll Make:

1st Avenue Power is growing its project development capacity, and we're looking for an Electrical Design Engineer to support the execution of solar and battery storage projects. This role is a great fit for someone who enjoys turning technical direction into concrete design deliverables, and who wants to build deep, hands-on experience across project and product engineering.

You'll work closely with our Power Electronics Engineering team, taking on drafting, modeling, feasibility, and layout work that helps the team move projects from concept to execution more quickly.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Create site layouts and electrical drawings based on direction from the engineering team
  • Conduct feasibility studies for new project and product concepts, applying prior experience to new sites and products
  • Develop early-stage design packages that help establish build standards and support oversight of EPC execution
  • Contribute to cost estimates that help the development team make go/no-go decisions

  • Support safety and stress testing, including fault current analysis and battery layout optimization

Nice to Have:

  • Knowledge of public utility and AHJ processes and approvals

title: Embedded Software Engineer
description:
Job Description: Senior Embedded Software Engineer

Location: SFO Bay area / Hybrid

Industry: Clean energy/ Software

1st Avenue Power (1AP) is creating a future where every nation, business, and community thrives with limitless access to cheap, reliable clean power. We deliver rapidly deployable power systems that generate Hyperfirm™ inexpensive clean energy, leveraging the abundance of solar to liberate energy-constrained industries like hyperscale datacenters.

As our first Embedded Software Engineer, you will be given a clean slate to architect and build the Embedded layer of a next-generation utility-scale power system. This is a high-agency role for any Engineer who wants to build software that controls massive amounts of energy in the physical world. You will take ownership of initial architectural decisions, from the communication stack to cloud telemetry, building an ecosystem without the burden of legacy technical debt.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • System Integration: Design and deploy comprehensive software solutions for supervisory control, OTA updates, telemetry, and manufacturing self-test protocols across solar, storage, and load subsystems.
  • Hardware Interfacing: Develop low-level drivers and communication stacks for power electronics using RS232/RS485, Modbus RTU, and CANbus to ensure seamless hardware-to-software connectivity.
  • Lead board bring-up efforts, ensuring hardware-firmware integration from power-on to full functionality.
  • Conduct comprehensive microcontroller and peripheral evaluations to select optimal components for system performance.
  • Architect and maintain robust device infrastructure, including secure bootloaders, automated firmware provisioning, and system diagnostics.
  • Safety-Critical Logic: Engineer high-reliability monitoring systems for arc fault detection and thermal management, implementing rapid software responses to hardware-level interrupts and fault signals.
  • Architecture: Take ownership of initial decisions for Linux-based gateways and communication layers from a clean slate.
  • Real-Time Control: Develop, enhance, and debug new and existing real-time software in embedded Linux and RTOS environments.
  • Validation: Drive a test-driven mentality where unit testing, software-in-the-loop (SIL), and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) are as important as developing new firmware.
  • Collaboration: Work with hardware teams to co-design optimal solutions for low-latency control, signal conditioning (level shifting), and system stability in high-noise DC environments.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Education: BS or MS in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
  • Languages: Proficiency in modern C/C++, with a strong preference for Rust or Go in high-concurrency systems.
  • Experience: 5+ years of hands-on experience in embedded systems, specifically with complex, physical hardware products from prototype to production.
  • Embedded Fundamentals: Experience with board bring-up, bootloaders, and kernel/driver development on embedded Linux or RTOS platforms.
  • Power Electronics: Proven experience in the control and monitoring of power conversion systems, including inverters, converters, and battery management systems (BMS).
  • Power Electronics & Protocols: Proven experience in the control and monitoring of power conversion systems (inverters, BMS) and a strong grasp of system-level power architecture and communication protocols (Modbus, CANbus, SPI, I2C).
  • Hardware Literacy: Ability to read schematics and understand signal conditioning (e.g., interfacing +/-12V RS232 signals with 3.3V MCUs) and the use of optoisolators for noise immunity.
  • Domain Knowledge: Basic understanding of Utility grid electrical architectures, MPPT charging algorithms, and power electronics concepts.
  • Hardware/Diagnostic Skills: Advanced proficiency in using laboratory equipment (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers) for hardware debugging and system-level troubleshooting.

Why Join Us?

  • Impact: Your code will directly manage renewable energy flow, helping stabilize the power grid.
  • Ownership: No technical debt. No "we’ve always done it this way." You set the standard.
  • Growth: As one of the first hires, you will play a foundational role in building the engineering culture and team.

California Pay Range
$120,000-$195,000 USD

title: Senior Hardware Design Engineer
description:
Sr. HW Design Engineer

The Impact You’ll Make:

We are looking for a talented and innovative Hardware Design Engineer with significant experience in TDR Equipment Design Engineer to join our R&D team. In this role, you will lead the design, development, and validation of Time Domain Reflectometry instruments and systems tailored for renewable energy applications — including solar PV, wind, and battery energy storage systems (BESS). You will work across the full hardware development lifecycle, from concept and schematic design through to prototyping, testing, and production handover. This is a technically deep, hands-on role ideal for an engineer passionate about precision measurement instrumentation and power systems diagnostics.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Hardware Design & Development

    • Design and develop TDR hardware including pulse generation circuits, high-speed analog front ends, sampling circuits, and signal conditioning stages
    • Design PCB layouts for high-frequency, low-noise TDR circuits using tools such as Altium Designer, or Cadence
    • Select and evaluate components including ADCs, DACs, op-amps, FPGAs, and microcontrollers suitable for TDR applications
    • Develop impedance matching networks and transmission line interfaces for various cable types (coax, twisted pair, MV power cables)
    • Design power supply and protection circuitry compliant with safety and EMC standards

    Signal Processing & Firmware

    • Collaborate with firmware/embedded engineers to develop DSP algorithms for TDR waveform acquisition, averaging, and fault-distance calculation
    • Define requirements for FPGA or microcontroller-based acquisition systems
    • Develop calibration routines and compensation algorithms to ensure measurement accuracy across temperature and load conditions
    • Contribute to real-time signal processing pipeline design for sub-nanosecond pulse resolution

    Prototyping & Validation

    • Build and test hardware prototypes in the lab — hands-on bench work with oscilloscopes, VNAs, spectrum analyzers, and signal generators
    • Conduct design verification testing (DVT) and design validation testing (DVT) across full environmental and electrical specifications
    • Perform EMC pre-compliance testing and support formal EMC/EMI certification
    • Validate TDR accuracy against reference cables and known fault conditions
    • Support field trials on renewable energy sites to validate performance under real-world conditions

    Standards & Documentation

    • Ensure designs comply with relevant standards including IEC 61010, IEC 61000 (EMC), and ISO 9001 quality requirements
    • Produce detailed design documentation including schematics, BOMs, design rationale, and test reports
    • Maintain version-controlled design files and contribute to IP/patent documentation where applicable
    • Support production engineering during design transfer and manufacturing ramp-up

    Collaboration & Innovation

    • Work closely with software, firmware, mechanical, and product management teams in an agile development environment
    • Engage with customers and field engineers to gather requirements and validate designs against real-world needs
    • Stay current with advances in TDR technology, high-speed analog design, and renewable energy diagnostics
    • Contribute to patent filings and technical publications where appropriate

The Skills You Bring:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a closely related discipline
  • 5+ years of experience in analog/mixed-signal hardware design, ideally in instrumentation or test & measurement
  • Strong proficiency in PCB design — schematic capture and layout using Altium Designer, or equivalent
  • Solid understanding of high-speed analog circuit design — signal integrity, transmission line theory, impedance matching
  • Hands-on experience with lab instruments: oscilloscopes, VNAs, spectrum analyzers, signal generators
  • Familiarity with TDR principles — pulse generation, reflection analysis, fault-distance calculation
  • Experience writing or reviewing hardware test plans and design verification reports

Nice to Have:

  • Direct experience designing TDR, OTDR, or reflectometry-based instrumentation
  • FPGA design experience (Xilinx / Intel) for high-speed data acquisition
  • Knowledge of cable types used in renewable energy — DC string cables, MV AC feeders, armored underground cables
  • EMC design experience and familiarity with IEC 61000 / FCC Part 15 test processes
  • Experience with SPICE simulation tools (LTspice, or similar)
  • Familiarity with IEC 61010 safety standard for electrical test & measurement equipment
  • Exposure to ISO 9001 or IEC 62443 (industrial cybersecurity for instrumentation)
  • Master's degree or PhD in relevant electronics/instrumentation field

title: Sr. Grid Integration Engineer
description:
Sr. Grid Integration Engineer

Location: Mountain View/San Jose Bay Area
Team: System Engineering

The Impact You’ll Make:

As a Sr. Grid Integration Engineer, you will architect the software and control fabric that turns our power conversion hardware, energy storage, and balance-of-plant equipment into a single, dispatchable power plant. You will build the EMS/PPC layer that sits above our PCS, MPPTs, batteries, meters, and switchgear — defining how every device talks, how setpoints flow from the grid operator down to the silicon, and how the plant behaves under every operating condition the grid can throw at it. This is a high-agency role where your concept of operations, sequence diagrams, and control logic become the operating system of our power plants.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Architect and build the Energy Management System (EMS) and Power Plant Controller (PPC) software stack that orchestrates inverters, MPPTs, battery systems, meters, and balance-of-plant equipment as a single grid-interactive plant.
  • Own the plant Concept of Operations — author sequence diagrams, state machines, and control narratives that describe power flow under every operating mode (PV-only, charging, discharging, curtailment, frequency response, voltage regulation, black start, night-mode transitions, fault ride-through).
  • Integrate power electronics (inverters, MPPTs, DC-DC converters), revenue and protection-class meters, BOP equipment, and PV systems into a unified software fabric using industry-standard protocols: DNP3, IEC 61850 (MMS, GOOSE, Sampled Values), Modbus TCP/RTU, SunSpec Modbus, MESA-ESS, IEEE 2030.5 (CSIP), OPC UA, and CAN.
  • Develop plant-level control logic for active power dispatch, reactive power / voltage support, ramp-rate control, frequency response (PFR / AGC), autonomous curtailment, and setpoint coordination across all device classes.
  • Implement and tune grid-following and grid-forming control strategies at the plant level — coordinating inverter modes, virtual inertia, droop response, and ride-through behavior between the PPC and underlying device controls.
  • Build the SCADA architecture for the plant: HMI, historian, alarms, event logging, time synchronization (PTP / IRIG-B), redundancy, and cybersecurity hardening (IEC 62443, NERC CIP awareness).
  • Develop control logic on SEL RTAC, Codesys (IEC 61131-3) PLCs, and model-based platforms (MATLAB / Simulink) — moving cleanly from simulation to deployable runtime code.

title: Sr. Reliability Engineer
description:
Sr. Reliability Engineer

Location: Mountain View/San Jose Bay Area
Team: System Engineering

The Impact You’ll Make:

We are seeking an experienced Senior Reliability Engineer to define and lead the reliability strategy for next-generation renewable energy products, including utility-scale photovoltaic systems, battery energy storage systems (BESS), power conversion systems (PCS), high-voltage power electronics, intelligent energy management systems, and supporting infrastructure. This individual will own reliability engineering from architecture through field deployment, ensuring products meet aggressive performance, availability, warranty, and 20+ year lifetime objectives.

The successful candidate will partner with Hardware, Firmware, Systems, Validation, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Product Management, and Field Service teams to proactively eliminate failure mechanisms, develop accelerated qualification plans, improve product robustness, and drive continuous reliability growth using data-driven engineering practices.

Key Responsibilities:

Reliability Strategy & Product Development

  • Own the reliability strategy across the complete product lifecycle.
  • Define quantitative reliability requirements, availability targets and warranty objectives.
  • Develop mission profiles representing utility-scale solar, BESS, microgrid and data-center applications.
  • Lead reliability design reviews and reliability sign-off before production.

Reliability Engineering & Modeling

  • Weibull analysis, MTBF/MTTF, Reliability Block Diagrams (RBD), Fault Tree Analysis (FTA).
  • Physics of Failure (PoF), stress-strength analysis, derating, reliability growth modeling.
  • Predict product lifetime using analytical and field data.

Accelerated Life Testing

  • Develop HALT, HASS and ALT programs.
  • Plan thermal cycling, power cycling, humidity, thermal shock, vibration, shock, salt fog, UV, ingress protection and endurance testing.
  • Correlate accelerated testing to expected field life.

Power Electronics & Energy Systems

  • Lead reliability for PV inverters, PCS, DC/DC converters, battery systems, SiC MOSFETs, IGBTs, capacitors, magnetics, busbars, contactors, sensors and cooling systems.
  • Evaluate electrical, thermal and mechanical failure mechanisms.

Failure Analysis

  • Lead structured root cause investigations using 8D, Fishbone, 5-Why and FTA.
  • Coordinate SEM, EDS, X-ray, CT scanning, cross-sectioning and thermal imaging.
  • Drive corrective/preventive actions and verify effectiveness.

Validation & Qualification

  • Create DVP&R and reliability qualification plans.
  • Review supplier qualification and production validation.

Field Reliability & Analytics

  • Analyze warranty, fleet, manufacturing and field-return data.
  • Develop reliability dashboards and KPIs.
  • Identify trends and prioritize design improvements.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Mentor junior engineers.
  • Interface with customers, suppliers and certification agencies.
  • Influence design decisions using reliability data.

The Skills You Bring:

  • BS or MS in Electrical, Mechanical, Reliability Engineering or related discipline.
  • 8+ years in reliability engineering for renewable energy, power electronics, industrial power systems or electrification.
  • Experience with accelerated life testing, statistical reliability and failure analysis.
  • Experience with DFMEA, PFMEA, DRBFM and root cause methodologies.
  • Strong communication and technical leadership.

Nice to Have:

  • ASQ Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE).
  • Six Sigma Green/Black Belt.
  • Utility-scale solar or BESS experience.
  • Knowledge of SiC-based power electronics.
  • Experience with ReliaSoft Weibull++, JMP, Minitab, MATLAB or Python.

About the Tech Stack

  • Standards: UL 1741, UL 62109, UL 9540, UL 9540A, IEEE 1547, IEC 62477, IEC 60068, IEC 62093.
  • Test equipment: power analyzers, oscilloscopes, thermal chambers, vibration systems, environmental chambers, DAQ.
  • Design tools: MATLAB, Python, JMP, Minitab, Weibull++, Altium (preferred).

About 1st Avenue Power:

At 1st Avenue Power, we are on a mission to deliver simple, fast-to-deploy, customer-centric and intelligent power systems leveraging the abundance of solar to provide inexpensive and reliable clean energy to global customers from data centers to energy starved communities around the world. We envision a future where every community, business, and nation thrives on the limitless potential of clean energy, united in a shared commitment to a sustainable and equitable world.

You will be working with Dr. Tom Buttgenbach, one of the most successful clean energy technology innovators and entrepreneurs who has been a driving force in making solar-based energy solutions the cheapest and most reliable energy option. Tom founded and led Avantus (formerly known as “8minute Solar Energy“), to become one of the largest and most profitable solar and energy storage companies in the United States and the largest in California, including delivering over 17% of Los Angeles’ power.

When Tom sold his interest in Avantus’ development business to KKR in mid-2024, it had delivered over $1 billion in profit and secured over $10 Billion in power purchase agreements and project financings with a pipeline of over 30 GW of solar and 90 GWh of energy storage, capable of powering the homes of more than 20 million Americans day and night.

Tom’s family office investment firm, 1st Avenue Capital, is building teams for the next generation of advanced solar power system architecture and AI to aggressively drive down the cost of and equitable access to clean and reliable energy.[1] 1st Avenue’s advanced large scale power systems are addressing the increasing inadequacy of the grid to meet the massively growing power demands of the digital economy, while its intelligent distributed solar utilities are leapfrogging the grid to provide equitable access to inexpensive, clean and reliable power to underserved communities around the world.
